A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a novel, potent, and selective series of mGlu5 PAMs was developed that led to the identification of 17a (JNJ-46778211), an orally bioavailable mGlu5 modulator that was advanced for further development as a clinical candidate for the treatment of schizophrenia.
we discovered a new chemical class of mGlu5 PAMs that are orally bioavailable and efficacious in preclinical models of schizophrenia.
the 2(phenoxylmethyl)oxazolo[4,5-c]pyridinyl-6,7-diphenol scaffold is a novel and useful template for the discovery of mGlu5 PAMs with good oral bioavailability and in vivo activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxazole ring can be used as a scaffold to design mGlu5 PAMs with good pharmacokinetic properties.
a novel series of 2-phenoxymethyl-6,7-dioxyazolo[5-4-c]pyrindinones were found to have potent and selective mGlu5 PAM activity.
a 6,7-dioxazolo ring system can be used in place of the 6,7-oxazolo system in mGlu5 PAMs.
